title: Egg whisk
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the 2016 page 44 hand-cranked double egg whisk sits over a bowl. Crank turns the large double-sided crown wheel and two smaller bevel pinions engaging its opposite faces, so both beaters spin faster than the handle and in opposite directions. Speed up increases only the hand-crank rate while preserving the fixed gear ratio. Lift is a teaching hand raising the whole tool out of the mixture, not a built-in lift. See-through reveals the crown wheel's two toothed faces, both pinions, their shafts, the supporting frame and the two beaters. Do not substitute an electric mixer, same-direction outputs or an invented speed selector.
blurb: A teaching adaptation of the hand-cranked egg whisk shows opposite crown-wheel faces driving two faster, counter-rotating beaters.

adaptation.scope: Teaching adaptation of 2016 page 44 and the 1998 Egg Beater alias, not an exact reconstruction or verified edition union.
adaptation.ratio: Illustrative fixed 32:8 tooth ratio, not measured from the source.
adaptation.controls: Speed up changes only hand input rate; Lift moves the holding hand and whole tool; Reset restores the teaching specimen.

editions.2016: direct page image and OCR support
